```{r setup, include=FALSE}
suppressPackageStartupMessages({library(knitr); library(kableExtra)})
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
source("../06_appendix_sources/cite.R")   # numbered citations: cite("key")
# master builder table (the same file Driver 4 reads), so the primer and Driver 4 always agree
mb <- read.csv("../data_ready/builders_latest_quarter.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
mb <- mb[match(c("D.R. Horton", "Lennar", "PulteGroup", "NVR", "KB Home", "Meritage Homes", "Toll Brothers"), mb$builder), ]
mb_w  <- mb$rev_musd / sum(mb$rev_musd)                     # revenue weights
ord_w <- sum(mb_w * mb$orders_yoy_pct)                      # revenue-weighted orders, % y/y
gm_w  <- sum(mb_w * mb$gm_change_bps)                       # revenue-weighted gross-margin change, bps
pct1  <- function(x) sprintf("%+.1f%%", x)
bps10 <- function(x) sprintf("%+.0f bps", 10 * round(x / 10))
d3 <- read.csv("../03_costs/outputs/d3_bridge_numbers.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
d3v <- function(n) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d3$value[d3$name == n]))
d2 <- read.csv("../02_inventory/outputs/d2_key_numbers.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
d2v <- function(n) suppressWarnings(as.numeric(d2$value[d2$name == n]))
com3 <- read.csv("../03_costs/outputs/d3_filing_commentary.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE, fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")
n_land <- sum(tolower(as.character(com3$cites_land_or_lot_cost)) == "true")   # builders citing higher land or lot costs
n_close_down <- sum(mb$closings_yoy_pct < 0)                                   # builders with closings down y/y
NAVY <- "#1f3350"; RED <- "#b5524f"
# bordered grid (light grey rules on every cell), navy header, bold first column: same look as the driver sections
# column_spec with cell text centred vertically (needs kableExtra 1.2+; falls back to top-aligned on older versions)
col_spec <- function(...) if ("latex_valign" %in% names(formals(kableExtra::column_spec))) kableExtra::column_spec(..., latex_valign = "m") else kableExtra::column_spec(...)
styled <- function(df, align, widths, bold_first = TRUE, font_size = 8) {
  k <- kable(df, format = "latex", booktabs = FALSE, align = align, escape = TRUE) %>%
    kable_styling(latex_options = "HOLD_position", font_size = font_size, full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#1f3350")
  n <- length(widths)
  for (i in seq_len(n)) k <- col_spec(k, i, width = paste0(widths[i], "cm"), bold = bold_first && i == 1,
                                         border_left = i == 1, border_right = i == n)
  k
}
strip_tbl <- function(labels, values, colors = rep(NAVY, length(values))) {
  cells <- mapply(function(v, c) cell_spec(v, "latex", bold = TRUE, color = c, font_size = 15), values, colors)
  df <- as.data.frame(setNames(as.list(unname(cells)), labels), check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  k <- kable(df, format = "latex", booktabs = TRUE, align = "c", escape = FALSE, linesep = "") %>%
    kable_styling(latex_options = "hold_position", font_size = 8.5, full_width = FALSE, position = "center") %>%
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE, color = "white", background = "#1f3350")
  for (i in seq_along(values)) k <- column_spec(k, i, width = "3.2cm")
  k
}

\vspace{3pt}
\begin{callout}
```

Mortgage rates have risen from 6.0% in March 2026 to 7.18% in early November 2026, limiting affordability and forcing builders to rely on more price cuts and continued incentives, such as mortgage-rate buydowns, to maintain sales volumes. These measures compress gross margins but also help builders gradually reduce excess inventory.

```{=latex}
\end{callout}
\vspace{3pt}
```

```{r players}
df <- data.frame(
  Builder = c(mb$builder, "Total"),
  `Revenue ($bn)` = c(sprintf("%.1f", mb$rev_musd / 1000), sprintf("%.1f", sum(mb$rev_musd) / 1000)),
  `Primary buyer tier` = c("Entry-level / first move-up", "First-time / first move-up", "First-time, move-up, active adult",
                           "First-time / move-up", "Entry-level / first move-up", "Entry-level / first move-up", "Luxury / affluent", "Total closings; weighted orders and margin"),
  `Closings y/y` = c(pct1(mb$closings_yoy_pct), pct1(100 * (sum(mb$closings) / sum(mb$closings_prior) - 1))),
  `Orders y/y` = c(pct1(mb$orders_yoy_pct), pct1(ord_w)),
  `Gross margin y/y` = c(bps10(mb$gm_change_bps), bps10(gm_w)),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
styled(df, align = c("l", "r", "l", "r", "r", "r"), widths = c(2.8, 2.0, 4.8, 2.0, 2.0, 2.6)) %>%
  row_spec(8, bold = TRUE, background = "#e8eef6")

```

```{=latex}
\vspace{-8pt}
{\footnotesize\itshape\color{gray} Exhibit 1. Seven large public builders, latest quarter. Revenue = home-sales revenue (weighting only). Closings = homes delivered. Tier is the author's classification.}
```

These seven builders span every buyer tier, from entry-level volume builders like D.R. Horton and KB Home to Toll Brothers at the luxury end, and together booked about $`r sprintf("%.0f", sum(mb$rev_musd) / 1000)`bn in home-sales revenue last quarter. Read together, they give an industry-level picture, and the pressure is broad rather than company-specific: orders are down at `r sum(mb$orders_yoy_pct < 0)` of the seven (`r pct1(ord_w)` revenue-weighted) and gross margins are down at `r sum(mb$gm_change_bps < 0)` (`r bps10(gm_w)`).

```{r cycle}
# How pressure moves through a homebuilder.
df <- data.frame(
  Stage = c("Land", "Orders", "Backlog and closings", "Finished inventory", "Gross margin", "New starts"),
  `What happens` = c(
    "Builders buy land, or hold options to buy it, well before a home is sold",
    "A buyer signs a contract; orders show current demand",
    "Homes under contract are built and delivered; closings become revenue",
    "Homes completed before a buyer is found sit unsold",
    "What is left of the selling price after land and construction costs",
    "Builders decide how many new homes to begin"),
  `Why it matters now` = c(
    sprintf("%d of %d large builders report higher land or lot costs", n_land, nrow(mb)),
    sprintf("Builder orders are down %.1f%% as rates near 7%% cut the number of qualified buyers", abs(ord_w)),
    sprintf("Deliveries continue from earlier contracts, so activity slows gradually; closings are down at %s builders", if (n_close_down == nrow(mb)) paste("all", nrow(mb)) else paste(n_close_down, "of", nrow(mb))),
    sprintf("%.0fK finished unsold homes, %.0f%% above 2018-19; builders move them with price cuts and incentives", d2v("completed_for_sale_k"), d2v("completed_pct_above_2018_19_avg")),
    sprintf("Prices and incentives adjust faster than costs: gross margin is down %.0f bps", abs(10 * round(gm_w / 10))),
    "Permits are down 4.7%; builders are planning fewer homes to control future supply"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
styled(df, align = c("l", "l", "l"), widths = c(2.9, 6.0, 8.1))
```

```{r snapshot}
# Activity and supply: 2018-19 average (the report's baseline), the same month a year ago, and the latest month.
rd <- function(pat) { f <- sort(Sys.glob(pat)); x <- read.csv(f[length(f)], stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  names(x) <- c("date", "v"); x$date <- as.Date(x$date); x$v <- suppressWarnings(as.numeric(x$v)); x[!is.na(x$v), ] }
h4 <- read.csv("../04_margins/outputs/d4_history.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE); h4$date <- as.Date(h4$date)
ser <- list(
  `New-home sales`        = rd("../01_affordability/data/raw/HSN1F_*.csv"),
  `Permits`               = data.frame(date = h4$date, v = h4$permits)[!is.na(h4$permits), ],
  `New starts`            = data.frame(date = h4$date, v = h4$starts)[!is.na(h4$starts), ],
  `Finished unsold homes` = rd("../02_inventory/data/raw/NHFSEPCS_*.csv"),
  `Months' supply`        = rd("../01_affordability/data/raw/MSACSR_*.csv"))
snap_now <- min(as.Date(sapply(ser, function(x) as.character(max(x$date)))))   # latest month all five series have
snap_ya  <- seq(snap_now, length.out = 2, by = "-1 year")[2]
at   <- function(x, d) x$v[x$date == d]
base <- sapply(ser, function(x) mean(x$v[x$date >= as.Date("2018-01-01") & x$date <= as.Date("2019-12-01")]))
ya   <- sapply(ser, at, snap_ya); now <- sapply(ser, at, snap_now)
fk   <- function(x, i) ifelse(i == 5, sprintf("%.1f", x), sprintf("%.0fK", x))
yoy  <- 100 * (now / ya - 1); vb <- 100 * (now / base - 1)
df <- data.frame(
  Metric = names(ser),
  b = fk(base, 1:5), y = fk(ya, 1:5), n = fk(now, 1:5),
  `What it shows` = c(
    sprintf("Demand is weaker than a year ago (%s)", pct1(yoy[1])),
    sprintf("Builders are planning fewer homes (%s y/y)", pct1(yoy[2])),
    sprintf("Starts have not fallen yet (%s y/y; %s vs 2018-19)", pct1(yoy[3]), pct1(vb[3])),
    sprintf("%.0f%% above 2018-19: the excess builders must clear", vb[4]),
    sprintf("%.1f months above the 2018-19 norm", now[5] - base[5])),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(df)[2:4] <- c("2018-19 average", format(snap_ya, "%b %Y"), format(snap_now, "%b %Y"))
styled(df, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "l"), widths = c(3.6, 2.3, 1.8, 1.8, 7.5))
```

```{=latex}
\vspace{-8pt}
{\footnotesize\itshape\color{gray} Exhibit 2. Activity and supply. Sales, permits and starts are single-family, annual rates. The 2018-19 average is this report's baseline; the monthly figures are seasonally adjusted and subject to revision. Source: Census Bureau and HUD.}
\vspace{4pt}
```

Higher interest rates are working through each stage of the homebuilding cycle (figures in Exhibit 2). **Land:** costs are not adjusting down with demand; `r n_land` of `r nrow(mb)` large builders report higher land or lot costs. **Orders:** fewer buyers qualify at 7%+, so new-home sales are below a year ago and builder sentiment (HMI) has fallen to 29. `r cite("census_nrs", "nahb_hmi")` **Backlog and closings:** builders are still delivering homes from earlier contracts, so activity slows gradually rather than stopping: closings fell at all `r n_close_down` builders, by a median of `r sprintf("%.1f", abs(median(mb$closings_yoy_pct)))`%. **Finished inventory:** finished unsold homes and months' supply are well above 2018-19, so builders are using incentives and price cuts to move them. **Gross margin:** those price cuts and incentives compress margins, down `r sprintf("%.0f", abs(10 * round(gm_w / 10)))` bps across the seven large builders. **New starts:** builders are pulling fewer permits to control future supply, although starts have not fallen yet. `r cite("census_nrc")` The housing market is adjusting, not collapsing: builders are still selling homes, but at the cost of margin, as they work down excess inventory.

## Four drivers

```{r drivers}
df <- data.frame(
  Priority = c("1", "2", "3", "4"),
  Driver = c("Affordability is the binding constraint", "Inventory forces the discounting",
             "Costs are not providing relief", "Margins are where it all shows up"),
  `Current signal` = c("Rate up 118 bps since March to 7.18%; payment about $250/month higher",
                       "111K finished unsold homes, 54% above 2018-19; 65% of builders using incentives",
                       sprintf("Builders' cost per home %+.1f%% y/y, with input prices up %.1f%%", d3v("cost_per_home_yoy_median_pct"), d3v("goods_input_ppi_yoy_pct")),
                       sprintf("Seven builders: gross margin down %.0f bps, orders down %.1f%%", abs(10 * round(gm_w / 10)), abs(ord_w))),
  `Why it matters now` = c(
    "Fewer buyers qualify, so orders fall, incentives rise and margins shrink",
    "Rates will not clear finished homes, so builders do, with incentives and price cuts",
    "Lot and input costs stay high while revenue per home falls",
    "Incentives cut revenue while costs hold, so margin stays below last year"),
  check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
styled(df, align = c("c", "l", "l", "l"), widths = c(1.2, 3.6, 5.8, 6.0)) %>%
  row_spec(1, background = "#e8eef6")
```

```{=latex}
\vspace{-8pt}
{\footnotesize\itshape\color{gray} Sources: Freddie Mac PMMS `r cite("freddie_pmms")`; Census and HUD `r cite("census_nrs", "census_nrc")`; NAHB HMI `r cite("nahb_hmi")`; builder earnings releases and filings `r cite("dhi_8k")`-`r cite("tol_release")`.}
```

- **Affordability:** Mortgage rates near 7% leave the monthly payment about $250 higher than in March, so fewer buyers qualify and builders must sell with incentives.
- **Inventory:** With rates unlikely to clear the `r sprintf("%.0f", d2v("completed_for_sale_k"))`K finished unsold homes, up `r sprintf("%.0f", d2v("completed_pct_above_2018_19_avg"))`% from the 2018-19 average, builders have to clear them themselves through price cuts and incentives, which hurts profitability.
- **Costs:** Land, materials and labor are not getting cheaper, so lower revenue per home against costs that stay high results in reduced margin and income.
- **Margins:** Incentives hit revenue when costs continue to rise, negatively impacting margins.
